segments.label: Historical heading
segments.original:
CAP. LXVII.
EDITTO
Sospensio de’ Mercati di Nauona, e del non far Piazze in luogo alcuno se non di robbe comestibili da Vitto.
segments.english:
Chapter 67
Edict
Suspension of Navona’s markets and prohibition of markets anywhere except for edible provisions.

segments.label: Prohibited goods and penalties
segments.original: Con il presente Editto Monsig. Illustriss. Carlo Bonelli dell’vna, e l’altra Segnatura di Nostro Signore Referendario, di Roma, e suo Distretto Gouernatore Generale, e Vicecamerlengo, per ouuiare ad ogn’inconueniente, che potesse accadere in pregiuditio della publica salute, secondo anche la risolutione fattasi nella Sacra Congregatione della Sanità, con il presente Editto proibisce alli Ebrei, Regattieri, Calzolari, Scarpinelli, Giupponari, Retagliari, & ad ogni altra persona il portare à vendere in giorno di Mercato, nè in altro tempo in Nauona, nè in altre Piazze, e luoghi di Roma, nè in quelli comprarui panni, e robbe da vestire, ò da letto, ò per altro vso, nè nuoui, nè vecchi, Rami, Stagni, nè altri Mobili, nè di quelli farne mostra, nè piazze in detti luoghi, sotto pena à chi contrauerrà, oltre alla perdita delle dette robbe, della Galera, & anco dalla vita ad arbitrio.
segments.english: By this edict His Most Illustrious Lordship Carlo Bonelli, Referendary of both Signatures of Our Lord, Governor General of Rome and its district and Vice-Camerlengo, to prevent any occurrence harmful to public health and also in accordance with the Sacred Congregation of Health’s resolution, forbids Jews, secondhand dealers, shoemakers, shoe repairers, doublet makers, cloth-remnant dealers and every other person from bringing for sale, on market day or at any other time, to Navona or other squares and places in Rome, or buying there, textiles and goods for clothing, bedding or any other use, whether new or old, copperware, pewterware or other furnishings, or displaying them or holding markets in those places. Offenders incur, besides forfeiture of those goods, the galleys and even death at discretion.

segments.label: Food exemption
segments.original: Ma solo sia lecito à ciascheduno portarui à vendere, ò comprare robbe da vitto, e comestibili.
segments.english: Everyone shall be permitted only to bring for sale or to buy food and edible provisions there.

segments.label: Legal effect of publication
segments.original: E vuole, che il presente Editto affisso, e publicato ne’ luoghi soliti di Roma ogn’vno astringa, & oblighi, come se gli fusse personalmente intimato.
segments.english: Once posted and published at Rome’s customary places, this edict shall bind and oblige everyone as if personally notified.

segments.label: Date and place
segments.original: Dat. in Roma questo dì 1. Luglio 1656.

segments.label: Signature
segments.original: Gio: Andrea Genuense Not. per la Carità.
segments.english: Gio: Andrea Genuense, notary for the Carità.

notes.text: The printed subtitle reads “Sospensio”, an abbreviated or incomplete form retained here rather than silently completed. The prohibition covers new as well as used nonfood goods.

The source explicitly names Jews among the persons prohibited, alongside occupational groups and all other persons. The translation preserves this discriminatory historical wording. The food exemption prevents the order being read as a closure of every food market.
